items.titleEn: Gold is being treated ‘like an AI stock, which it's not,' says Peter Boockvar
items.summaryEn: The OnePoint BFG Wealth Partners CIO said gold ’s drop below $4,000 looked like forced selling. Days later, gold is back above $4,000 after the midterms, and he says investors shouldn’t count on the Fed to rescue the AI trade. NEW ORLEANS (Kitco News) - Gold fell more than $120 an ounce on Oct. 30 and broke below $4,000. To Peter Boockvar, it didn’t look like a broken thesis. It looked like a forced seller. “ Gold ’s not trading on its own fundamentals. There’s a forced seller out there, whether it’s margin-driven or whatever,” the chief investment officer at OnePoint BFG Wealth Partners told Kitco News at the New Orleans Investment Conference on Oct. 30.

Gold holding firm as US ISM says Service Sector expands in October
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - The gold market continues to hold critical support above $4,000 an ounce, but steady activity in the U.S. services sector highlights the ongoing challenges for the precious metal, as a resilient economy and persistent inflation give the Federal Reserve room to maintain its tightening bias. The Institute for Supply Management (ISM) announced Wednesday morning that its Services Purchasing Managers Index came in at 54.5 in October, down slightly from 54.9 in September. The data was modestly weaker than expected, as economists were looking for a roughly unchanged reading of 54.8. Although momentum in the services sector continues to slow, activity remains in expansion territory. Readings above 50 in such diffusion indexes signify economic growth, while readings below 50 indicate contraction. The farther an indicator is above or below 50, the greater the rate of expansion or contraction.

Gold and silver surge as Democratic midterm sweep drives dollar, yields lower - Kitco AM Report
items.summaryEn: (Kitco NewsWire) – Spot gold and silver prices were sharply higher in early U.S. trading Wednesday, as Democrats' sweeping victories in the U.S. midterm elections sent the dollar and Treasury yields lower, encouraging renewed buying interest in precious metals. The election results handed Democrats control of both the House of Representatives and Senate, raising expectations for legislative gridlock and potentially more restrained federal spending during the remainder of President Donald Trump's term. Gold climbed back above $4,000.00 an ounce following October's sharp correction, while silver recovered more strongly as lower yields and improved precious metals sentiment encouraged buying. At the time of writing, spot gold was trading near $4,041.30 an ounce, up $111.90, or 2.85%, while spot silver was trading near $51.910, up $2.237, or 4.50%, on the session. Tuesday's U.S. midterm elections produced a decisive shift in the balance of power in Washington, with Democrats securing majorities in both chambers of Congress. Democrats gained at least seven Senate seats and 18 House seats, including victories in states that supported Trump in the 2024 presidential election. The results significantly reduce the administration's ability to advance new fiscal, tax and regulatory legislation without congressional compromise, while raising the prospect of intensified oversight of federal spending and policies affecting artificial intelligence, energy and financial markets. However, majorities in Congress do not automatically translate into lower federal deficits, and any substantial change in the borrowing outlook will depend on the legislation ultimately enacted.

Gold prices holding $4,000 as ADP says US economy created 86k jobs in October
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - Gold prices are holding recent gains above $4,000 an ounce but could face renewed selling pressure as the U.S. labor market remains relatively healthy, with the economy creating more private-sector jobs than expected. ADP said Wednesday that 86,000 jobs were created in October, down from 90,000 jobs created in September. However, the data significantly beat expectations, as consensus estimates had forecast a gain of 67,000 jobs. The report noted that the labor market has shown solid growth for a second consecutive month, while pay gains have remained steady.
